content.text:
The smallest clear ownership shift is to compute groups in Rust during declaration loading and persist the result. The current recursive grouping lives in `funder_alias_groups`; search and details read that view from [funder.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs) and [entity_details.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed-transitive-alias-groups-20261012/exposed/src/lib/outbound/entity_details.rs).

After the loader upserts funders and aliases, Rust can normalize names, build alias and curated-family evidence edges, and run union-find over funder UUIDs. Assign each component its minimum UUID as the representative, including isolated funders. Persist one group row per funder and direct evidence rows for alias or family links. Search and details then join those tables; the recursive view is no longer needed.

Keep the reviewed family names and normalization rules together in a Rust domain module. Rebuild groups over all surviving funders in the loader transaction, since aliases can bridge existing components and stale IDs must not remain after pruning. A migration can backfill the new tables from the existing views before removing them; its down migration can restore the prior views and family seed table.

One key integration issue: repository tests insert or delete aliases directly and then query groups. Stored groups will be stale unless those paths trigger recomputation or the tests use a refresh path. Also account for family-config changes in the grouping version or fingerprint so unchanged input artifacts can still produce updated groups.
